comparison: Perfect agreement on background claims C7-C19. Both evaluations recognize these as well-established foundational knowledge about photosynthetic reaction centers, supported by appropriate literature citations. No challenges from either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on NSD analysis claims C5, C56-C61, C67. Both evaluations support the finding that expected saddling mode deformation is absent at 5 ps and 20 ps when HL•– should be present. Peer reviewer explicitly acknowledges this contradicts the XFEL structure interpretation.

Perfect agreement on computational methods C78-C93. Both evaluations accept the methodological approach as appropriate and rigorous. Peer reviewers describe calculations as 'systematic' and 'well prepared,' while OpenEval notes methods are standard with appropriate citations, though suggests some details could be more explicit.
Perfect agreement on forward-looking claims C74-C75. Both evaluations accept these as reasonable suggestions for future research based on identified limitations. No challenges from either evaluation.

Strong agreement on Em(HL) analysis claims C4, C48-C55 (90% overlap). Both evaluations support the finding that absence of expected Em(HL) stabilization at 5 ps and 20 ps indicates problems with XFEL structures. Peer reviewer explicitly states Em values 'are not clearly changed,' confirming the interpretation. OpenEval also includes C68 which peer review addresses separately.

Strong agreement on species-specific residue contributions C39-C47 (90% overlap). Both evaluations accept these detailed computational findings about residue-level contributions to energetic asymmetry. Peer reviewers implicitly accept through praise of 'systematic calculations,' while OpenEval explicitly validates the species comparisons.

Strong agreement on Em calculations and residue contributions C2-C3, C28-C33, C64-C65 (62.5% overlap). Both evaluations support the computational findings. Peer review also includes claims about branch asymmetry (C34-C38, C66) that OpenEval addresses in separate result R4. Both note good agreement with prior work and experimental data.

Partial agreement on branch asymmetry claims C34-C37, C66 (31.2% overlap). OpenEval addresses these separately while peer review groups them with broader Em calculations. Both evaluations support the identification of key residue pairs responsible for energetic asymmetry across species.

Strong agreement on characterization of Dods et al. study C1, C20-C24 (66.7% overlap). Both evaluations accept these as accurate representations of the prior XFEL work being evaluated. OpenEval also includes C25-C27 about data quality concerns, which peer review addresses in R5.

Partial agreement on XFEL data quality concerns C25-C27 (27.3% overlap). Both evaluations support the assessment that low resolution and noise in XFEL data are problematic. Peer reviewer explicitly agrees conformational changes at 2.8 Å resolution 'are not reliable enough.' Peer review also includes broader interpretation claims (C69, C73) addressed in OpenEval R9.

Moderate agreement on main conclusion claims C6, C70, C72 (33.3% overlap). Both evaluations strongly support the central conclusion that structural changes in XFEL structures are not related to actual charge separation. Peer reviewers explicitly state authors 'found no clear link' and changes 'may reflect experimental errors.' OpenEval also includes C68-C69, C73 which peer review addresses across multiple results.

Partial agreement on QA analysis claims C62-C63, C71 (37.5% overlap). Both evaluations support findings about absence of expected Em(QA) stabilization. Peer review groups these with broader conclusion claims (C6, C70, C72) that OpenEval addresses in R9. OpenEval also includes validation claims C76-C77 addressed in peer R9.

Partial agreement on computational validation C76-C77 (40% overlap). Both evaluations accept the validation of computational methods through comparison with experimental Em(QA) values. Peer reviewers implicitly accept through praise of 'systematic calculations,' while OpenEval explicitly notes this validates the computational approach.

Partial agreement on interpretation of data limitations C69, C73 (22.2% overlap). Both evaluations support the conclusion that observed changes may reflect experimental errors rather than real structural changes. Peer review also addresses data quality concerns (C25-C27) that OpenEval includes in R2.

Minimal overlap on claim C68 (6.7% overlap). Both evaluations support this claim about lack of correlation between structural changes and electron transfer signatures, though peer review groups it with Em(HL) analysis while OpenEval includes it in the main conclusion discussion.

Minimal overlap on claim C38 (4% overlap). Both evaluations support this claim about computational findings, though it represents a small connection between OpenEval's species-specific analysis and peer review's broader acceptance of Em calculations.
